description.value: A diffusion tensor imaging study investigating white matter microstructural abnormalities in unmedicated patients with obsessive-compulsive disorder compared with healthy controls, and changes after 12-week SSRI treatment.

spans.text: Parameter maps of DTI, including fractional anisotropy (FA), axial diffusivity (AD), radial diffusivity (RD) and mean diffusivity (MD), were acquired from 27 unmedicated OCD patients (including 13 drug-naïve individuals) and 23 healthy controls.

spans.text: We hypothesized that abnormalities of white matter microstructure including myelin integrity would be found in OCD patients. We also predicted that sufficient medication would normalize the changes in white matter microstructure.

description.value: The study had a baseline comparison of unmedicated OCD patients and healthy controls, with a 12-week SSRI treatment and follow-up DTI assessment in a subgroup of OCD patients.

spans.text: In the current study, we employed the DTI technique to study white matter abnormality in OCD patients using multiple parameters including FA, AD, RD and MD. These parameters were compared for patients before and after 12-week Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitor (SSRI) pharmacotherapy.

description.value: DTI volumes were corrected for eddy-current distortion, brain masked, tensor fitted, parameter maps normalized to a B0 template, and smoothed before statistical testing.

spans.text: The eddy current distortion was first corrected for each participant's DTI volume using the “eddycorrect” toolbox in FSL. Then, a brain mask, which separated brain and non-brain regions, was calculated from the B0 volume using the BET toolbox (FSL). Restricted within this mask, a diffusion tensor was fitted for each voxel in the brain image space using FSL's DTIFit. FA, AD, RD and MD maps were subsequently calculated.
All data were processed using SPM8 (  http://www.fil.ion.ucl.ac.uk/spm/  ), and FSL (  http://www.fmrib.ox.ac.uk/fsl/  ) on a Linux based platform.

The eddy current distortion was first corrected for each participant's DTI volume using the “eddycorrect” toolbox in FSL. Then, a brain mask, which separated brain and non-brain regions, was calculated from the B0 volume using the BET toolbox (FSL). Restricted within this mask, a diffusion tensor was fitted for each voxel in the brain image space using FSL's DTIFit.

Finally, following a popularly used schema - described in a previous study with OCD patients  [9]  - we smoothed all the transformed parameter maps with a 6-mm FWHM Gaussian kernel, ready for further statistical testing.
A General Linear Model repeated-measure analysis of covariance (ANOVA) was used in the analysis of each DTI-derived parameter before and after treatment.

We performed a whole-brain voxel-based analysis using the normalized and smoothed FA, AD, RD and MD maps for a 2-sample group t-test, comparing the 23 control participants and 27 patients before medication.
